architecture_overview: The system is a project management and sprint planning application for Product Owners (PO) and Scrum Masters (SM). It allows creating, tracking, and managing sprints, tasks, acceptance criteria, and team velocity metrics through a web interface. The architecture is based on a modular microservice approach with separate services for authentication, sprint planning, task management, and reporting. The frontend communicates via RESTful APIs with a backend based on Node.js and Express, backed by a PostgreSQL database. Redis is used for caching, and JWT-based authentication secures API calls. Docker and Kubernetes manage containerized deployments.

api_endpoints.description: Create a new sprint with defined goals, start/end dates, and associated tasks.
Retrieve sprint details including acceptance criteria and tasks.
Create a new task under a sprint with PO acceptance criteria.
Update task status as per SM sprint plan progress.
Retrieve team velocity and sprint completion metrics.

database_schema: CREATE TABLE sprints (id UUID PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(255), start_date DATE, end_date DATE, goals TEXT); CREATE TABLE tasks (id UUID PRIMARY KEY, sprint_id UUID REFERENCES sprints(id), title VARCHAR(255), description TEXT, acceptance_criteria TEXT[], assignee VARCHAR(255), status VARCHAR(50)); CREATE TABLE users (id UUID PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(255), role VARCHAR(50), email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE);
security_considerations: Use JWT tokens for authenticated API requests.
Enforce RBAC to distinguish PO, SM, and developer permissions.
Validate all API input through schema validation (e.g., Joi).
Encrypt sensitive data (passwords, tokens) using bcrypt.
Implement HTTPS/TLS for all network communications.
Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection.
code_structure: src/ ├── api/ │   ├── controllers/ │   ├── routes/ │   ├── middleware/ ├── models/ ├── services/ │   ├── sprintService.js │   ├── taskService.js │   ├── reportService.js ├── config/ │   ├── db.js │   ├── auth.js ├── utils/ ├── tests/
implementation_notes: Follow clean architecture principles—separate business logic from controllers. Use React functional components with hooks for state management and Redux for global state. Apply caching for frequently accessed sprint data via Redis. Implement CI/CD with Docker and Kubernetes, ensuring deployments are scalable. Logging and monitoring with Winston and Prometheus. Unit tests for services and integration tests for APIs with Jest and Supertest.
